title: Einstein's Letter
text: Einstein wrote to his friend Max Born in nineteen twenty-six that quantum mechanics was impressive,
nxt: but that an inner voice told him it was not yet the real thing. He was convinced, he wrote, that God does not throw dice.

title: Bohr's Reply
text: According to accounts passed down, Niels Bohr answered that Einstein should stop telling God what to do.
nxt: Whether or not those exact words were spoken, the argument was real. It was about whether nature is truly random.

title: A Decay With No Reason
text: Take an unstable atom such as carbon-fourteen. Physics can tell you the chance that it decays during the next hour with great precision.
nxt: But it cannot tell you when that one atom will go. In standard quantum theory, there is no hidden clock inside the nucleus.

title: Order From Chance
text: Even with random atoms, a chair stays solid.
nxt: Individual atoms behave probabilistically, but a chair contains an unimaginable number of them, so their average behavior is steady.

title: What Physics Cannot Say
text: So does quantum mechanics prove that God does not exist? No. Science can challenge particular arguments, such as a perfectly predictable universe.
nxt: It cannot rule out every idea of God, and physicists themselves hold a wide range of views.
